impacts.title: Scientific impact
impacts.claim: FIELDWISE provides a framework for agricultural AI evaluated according to temporal + geographic + operational transferability rather than only retrospective accuracy. It additionally establishes a methodological bridge between high-information proximal hyperspectral observations and scalable Sentinel-based prediction.

impacts.title: Environmental impact
impacts.claim: FIELDWISE contributes to the EU-level opportunity for water savings in irrigated agriculture by improving the timing and spatial prioritisation of irrigation decisions. The project does not claim in advance that it will achieve a particular percentage reduction; impact will be quantified from project evidence.

impacts.title: Agricultural and food-production impact
impacts.claim: Water scarcity already produces agricultural yield losses and higher water costs in Europe, while irrigation demand is expected to increase under climate change. Processing tomato provides a high-value horticultural test case in which improved timing can therefore have substantial agronomic and economic relevance.

impacts.title: Technological impact
impacts.claim: FIELDWISE advances the project from a desktop research prototype to a scientifically validated web MVP. External AgroVIR evaluation provides evidence about whether the resulting technology meets actual agricultural software requirements.

impacts.title: European impact
impacts.claim: The MATE-MVCRI architecture directly investigates whether agricultural AI developed in one European environment can be transferred to another. FIELDWISE therefore contributes to a wider European question: how can locally developed agricultural intelligence become reliably transferable rather than remaining confined to the field in which it was trained?

kpis.note: No KPI is lifted, because the draft carries none: it explicitly declines advance numeric targets and commits to quantifying impact from project evidence (¶243). expected_impact_coverage.note: phase_05_gate g06_p04 requires all six Tier 2B expected impacts to map to a project output. The draft's §2.3 covers EI-02 and EI-05, and §2.1/§2.2 cover EI-01. Nothing in the draft addresses EI-03 (public engagement), EI-04 (Charter alignment) or EI-06 (teaching). The operator decided all three in input pack item 5 (EI-03 candidate accepted; EI-04 accepted with the HRS4R claim removed per C8; EI-06 raised per C7); ticket 6 folds them. Until then the three mappings are Unresolved here, and Phase 5 would fail g06_p04 honestly if run first.
